events.title: Proposed ruling: refund_full $6.61 (model confidence 0.95)
events.body:
The trip is a driver-cancelled trip on which the driver claimed rider no-show, so the $6.61 cancellation fee is valid only if NS-1's three cumulative conditions are met; NS-0 routes the claim through NS-1 and nothing else [F3][F6][NS-0]. The fee therefore stands or falls with NS-1.

The GPS record settles NS-1(i)–(iii) against the driver. His closest approach to the pickup point in the whole window was 873 m and he never came within 200 m [F1]; at the moment of the "I'm Here" tap (22:37:20) he was 1000 m from the pickup point and spent 0 s inside the radius afterwards [F5], and the only long stationary stretch (22:37:00–22:42:00) was likewise 1000 m away [F2]. NS-1(ii) and (iii) therefore fail on the platform's own record, and the platform never logged an arrival at all (driver_arrived_at null) [F4][NS-1].

The driver's contrary material cannot rescue the fee. what_would_change: Had NS-1 (ii) and (iii) both held ((ii) within 200 m of pickup AT THE MOMENT of the arrival confirmation; (iii) stayed at the pickup more than 3 min after the arrival confirmation, until cancelling (NS-1 default: more than 3 min)), the fee would stand and no refund would be due.

claims.assertion: The driver never reached the pickup point: his closest approach was 873 m and he was never within 200 m, and the platform recorded no arrival (driver_arrived_at is null).
NS-1(ii) fails: the driver tapped "I'm Here" at 22:37:20 while 1000 m from the pickup point, so he was not at the pickup location according to GPS when he indicated arrival.
claims.void_reason: citation check: cites A3 — not a citable clause

claims.assertion: NS-1(iii) also fails: after the "I'm Here" tap the driver spent 0 s within 200 m of the pickup point, and his 5-minute stationary period (22:37:00–22:42:00) was 1000 m away, so there was no continuous 3-minute wait at the pickup point.

The driver's own GPS and his chat message are irreconcilable: he wrote "Reached already" at 22:37 while the record shows him stationary 1000 m from the pickup point, and he then cancelled at 22:42 citing a 3-minute wait that never occurred.

The rider was at the pickup point and said so at 22:38 — "I'm at the pickup point, no car here. Where are you?" — so the no-show did not occur; the chat record is complete (3 messages, all timestamped), so no evidence gap requires escalation.
The $6.61 cancellation fee recorded on the fare must therefore be refunded in full, since none of the NS-1 conditions for charging it is satisfied and the driver, not the rider, cancelled.

A flag_account action is warranted in addition: the driver pressed "I'm Here" while GPS placed him 1000 m from the pickup point, which is abuse of the cancellation/waiting button, and his profile shows 2 no-show disputes upheld in 90 days.

weaknesses: The driver's written statement (F12) asserts he pressed "I'm Here" and waited more than 3 minutes at the pickup; the judge must prefer the GPS/timeline records (F1, F2, F5) over this statement, but the statement is on the record for the other side.
The rider's own profile (F16) shows 1 dispute in 90 days with 0 upheld, which the driver could use to paint the rider as a repeat complainant with no merit.

Weather was light rain (F15), which the driver could raise as an excuse for stopping 1000 m away; there is no traffic incident or congestion record (F13, F14) to support a genuine blockage, but the rider has no positive evidence of where the rider physically stood at 22:37–22:42 beyond the chat message (F9).

If the driver's whereabouts after 22:42:00 are not fully covered by the track, he could argue the record is incomplete; the provided facts show no GPS gap, but the rider cannot affirmatively prove the absence of one.

claims.assertion: The cancellation fee of $6.61 was charged under the no-show route and cancels on the rider's side of the ledger, but NS-0 routes a driver-cancelled trip claiming rider no-show through NS-1, and NS-1's three cumulative requirements must all be recorded before the fee can stand; GPS shows the driver's closest approach to the pickup point was 873 m at 22:36:00 and he never came within 200 m, so NS-1(ii) is not satisfied.

The driver pressed "I'm Here" at 22:37:20 while positioned 1000 m from the pickup point and stayed within 200 m for 0 s after the tap, so both the arrival position requirement (NS-1(ii)) and the continuous waiting requirement (NS-1(iii)) fail on the platform's own record.

The platform never recorded the driver at the pickup point at all (driver_arrived_at is null), and the only stationary period in the track is 22:37:00-22:42:00 spent 1000 m away from the pickup point, so no arrival-at-pickup condition of NS-1 is met on the system record.

The driver's written statement that he "waited more than 3 minutes at the pickup" is contradicted by the GPS track showing the wait occurred 1000 m from the pickup point; under the system-record-wins rule that statement cannot establish NS-1(iii), and his chat message "Reached already" at 22:37 is equally undercut by F5.

The rider reported from the pickup point at 22:38 that no car was there, which is consistent with the GPS record that no vehicle came within 200 m of the pickup point during the whole window, so the rider's account is corroborated rather than contradicted by the system data.

Because the driver tapped "I'm Here" while GPS placed him 1000 m from the pickup point, NS-2's additional consequence attaches: the $6.61 is refunded in full AND the account is sent for Ryde review for abuse of the arrival/cancellation button; the driver's 90-day history (2 no-show disputes, 2 upheld, 808 trips) supports but does not by itself establish that flag.

No weather or traffic justification exists for the driver's inability to reach the pickup point: there were no traffic incidents near the route and no speed-band records in the trip window, and light rain of 1.8 mm is not evidence accepted under the policy for a route-related excuse.

weaknesses: The chat record is complete and fully timestamped (F11) and the driver did send a plausible-sounding "Reached already, blue Toyota Prius, come out please" at 22:37 (F8), which the other side will read as an arrival notification; F5 (tap 1000 m away, 0 s within 200 m) and F1 (never within 200 m) are the facts that defeat it.

The rider's own file is not clean: profile F16 shows 1 dispute in 90 days and a 4.4 rating, which the other side will use to argue the rider is a repeat complainant, though it shows 0 upheld no-show disputes.

The driver's account history is the most damaging fact for us: F17 records 2 upheld no-show disputes in 90 days, which the other side will use to argue a pattern and which strengthens the NS-2 flag_account request rather than defeating it.

RD-6's "repeated" counting window is an open policy gap (G4), so relying on F17 to escalate is an overlay on a rule Ryde has not published a counting standard for; the primary flag basis is NS-2's button-abuse provision, which stands on F5 alone.

points.response: Agreed and adopted: NS-0 routes this driver-cancelled no-show claim through NS-1, and the 873 m closest approach in F1 means NS-1(ii) is never met, so the fee cannot stand.
Agreed: the 22:37:20 tap recorded 1000 m from the pickup point (F5) and 0 s spent within 200 m afterwards defeat both NS-1(ii) and NS-1(iii), independently of the stationary period in F2.
Agreed: with driver_arrived_at null (F4) and the only long stop spent 1000 m away (F2), no arrival condition of NS-1 is met on the system record.

Agreed, and I go further: the driver's statement (F12) and his "Reached already" message (F8) both fail against the GPS record of a 1000 m stop (F2) and a tap made 1000 m out (F5), so neither can establish NS-1(iii).
Agreed: the rider's 22:38 message (F9) is corroborated by F1, since no vehicle came within 200 m of the pickup point in the whole window.
Agreed on both limbs: the tap 1000 m away (F5) triggers NS-2's full $6.61 refund plus the account flag, and F17's 2 upheld no-show disputes support but do not decide that flag.
Agreed: with no incidents near the route (F14) and no speed-band records (F13), light rain of 1.8 mm (F15) is no excuse and the driver has no justification for stopping a kilometre short.

Clarification of my own claim, matching the driver's own weakness note: the flag rests on NS-2's button-abuse provision and F5 alone, not on RD-6's unpublished 90-day counting window (G4); F17 is support only.

Conceded — the GPS record (F1: closest approach 873 m, never within 200 m) and the absent platform arrival (F4: driver_arrived_at null) establish that NS-1(i) and NS-1(ii) fail; this is our own D1/D3 and we do not contest it.

Conceded — F5 (tap at 22:37:20, 1000 m out, 0 s within 200 m after) and F2 (5 min stationary 1000 m away) mean NS-1(iii)'s continuous in-range wait is not met, so the $6.61 cannot stand; this matches our D2.

Conceded as to the finding, with one correction: the driver's contradictory message F8 and statement F12 are defeated by F2/F5, and the 22:41 message F10 shows he himself relied on a 3-minute wait that the track does not support — the system record controls.

Conceded — F9 (rider at the pickup point at 22:38) plus the complete, timestamped chat F11 means no evidence gap under G12; we do not seek escalation on that basis, and F1 independently corroborates that no vehicle came within 200 m.

Conceded — NS-0 routes this driver-cancelled no-show claim through NS-1, and because NS-1 fails the $6.61 must be refunded in full under NS-2; the amount is exactly the cancellation fee recorded at F6, so refund_full $6.61 is common ground.

The button-abuse flag is expressly available under NS-2 on F5 alone (tap at 1000 m), but the profile citation should be corrected: F17 shows 2 no-show disputes upheld in 90 days and the rider's own F16 shows 0 upheld, so the record supports the flag without needing the rider's profile.
